positive.prompt: We added a field to the new files last month, but it isn't showing up when I read the folder.
Finance needs a few rows corrected, and rewriting the file each time is getting dangerous. What should the storage be?
Two jobs are going to write into the same dataset folder from now on. Is that going to hold?

negative.prompt: Give me revenue per channel for the last quarter and the quarter before it, from these parquet tables.
Chart the monthly revenue from this CSV; the amounts came in as text with comma decimals.

evals.prompt: We started recording a refund reason on the events a month ago. Give me refunds by reason across everything in events/.
evals.expected_output: The refunds by reason, plus the fact that a plain read of the directory does not return the column at all and why.
expectations: The response establishes that the refund_reason column exists in one file and not the others, by inspecting the files rather than trusting a single read of the directory
It states that a plain read of the directory drops the column silently, with no error, and explains that the schema comes from the first file in name order
The answer it gives for refunds by reason is scoped to the rows that actually carry the column, rather than presented as covering all three months
It does not report that the column is missing from the data, which would be a claim about the files that the files contradict

evals.prompt: From next month two jobs will write into events/ at the same time, and finance wants order 1 corrected rather than duplicated. Should we move this to a table format?
evals.expected_output: A recommendation grounded in the needs that a directory cannot meet, with the cost of the move named.
expectations: The recommendation is justified by what the directory cannot do, naming the concurrent writers, the row-level correction and the schema change, rather than by the size of the data
The duplicate of order 1 is found in the files and used as the concrete example of a correction the layer cannot express
The cost is named, including that reader support for the format is fetched over the network on first use and is not installed by default
Compaction or partitioning is addressed as work somebody has to own, rather than presented as coming for free with the format
